findings.claim: 19 canonical module slugs, including three core presentation/platform entries.
findings.implication: Preserve IDs; separate customer vocabulary from internal module identities.

findings.claim: Retailer/services presets and existing configuration UI already implement part of workflow composition.
findings.implication: Extend the existing composer; adoption benefit still requires a user study.

findings.claim: Configuration, grants, commands and lifecycle evidence are separate models.
Preview hashes, revisions, actor scope and idempotency protect configuration changes.
findings.implication: Preserve and validate integrated transaction behavior.

findings.claim: Low-level default observes; specific transports enforce; item creation explicitly observes before its service.
limitations: No live exploit or entire-surface coverage claim
Item-create finding is source-level; no new real record created
findings.implication: Complete the commercial enforcement map before monetized restrictions; no global mode switch.

findings.claim: Composer explicitly has no-purchase semantics and preserves existing legacy grants; commercial provider provisioning not demonstrated.
limitations: Search scope: current services, actions, app/api, schema and module reports; not a universal absence claim
findings.implication: Treat package purchase/provisioning as separately specified work.

findings.claim: Inventory, purchasing, payroll and manual-journal stop supported; sales/POS/direct reconciliation stop unsupported.
Catalog entries and actual destinations differ; reports requires analytics eligibility in destination mapping.
limitations: Missing composition destination is not proof of absent domain functionality
findings.implication: Reconcile advertised scope and hidden prerequisites.

findings.claim: Readiness checks use actual accounting, terminals, providers, payroll period and restricted compliance scope.
limitations: No production provider or statutory certification
findings.implication: Retain scope-specific readiness and explain it to users.

findings.claim: Eligibility, readiness, destination, recipe and operational dependencies are defined separately.
findings.implication: Validate consistency while preserving distinct dependency meanings.

findings.claim: Several historical resolver defects are corrected in current functions.
limitations: Isolated real-function execution with stubs; no full-system claim
findings.implication: Do not reopen corrected work based only on old reports.

findings.claim: Retained admission policy is distinct from suspended/expired grant read access.
findings.implication: Future commercial cancellation must deliberately preserve defined retained authority rather than merely retain rows.

findings.claim: C foundation plus bounded D1 experience is the preferred incremental direction.
findings.implication: Run the purchasing recipe experiment before broader investment.

findings.claim: A small bundle menu or broad-suite plan may be clearer than per-internal-module charges.
findings.implication: Compare commercial prototypes and costs; do not set production prices from this audit.

jest.scope: Existing tests; persistence/session test doubles; bounded CJS configuration
